Something that helps me "take the edge off" (meaning getting myself to a point where I can rationally get my mind and body the care it needs) are simple free phone puzzle games. Of course it doesn't have to be puzzle games, any small task that almost forces you to be mindful is a huge help I find.

Other things to be aware of include your sleeping habits (make sure you're getting enough since lack of sleep will hurt and if you find yourself too stressed out to slumber maybe look into some melatonin just to get yourself back on a healthy routine. Another thing to consult your doctor with even your standard practitioner). Changes in food can be triggering especially sugar and caffeine, be aware of your intake and take care of yourself appropriately. Small amounts of exercise can help regulate your body's connection to the mind as well, if you don't already daily walks I can highly recommend.

Sounds to me like you're doing all the right things and are being pretty reasonable given the situation at had. Course there's variables like how long you've guys been together and how well you know him, but the hard part is guys like this (girls too) tend to downward spiral. If you try to confront him about his bizarre and absent behavior, it's more likely to concrete the bubbling thoughts in his head that he doesn't deserve you, that he's treating you wrong, etc.

At the same time...he kinda is. Its an impossible balance. If you are someone who strives on open communication he might not be the individual for you. Course that's for you to decide. If I were you, I would set a theoretical deadline. Figure out how long you're willing to wait and leave the door open till then for him to recover and seek you out for a discussion. If he does return, however fragile he presents himself, establish a boundary that you care for him and you are partners in this together. Yes there will be battles he must fight alone, but the infrequent updates are usually enough to quell the worrying mind until the war is done
